subject: Hosted API evaluation — prefetch, endpoint mapping, and ratecap playbook
messages:
From: Alec Chen <alec@retaillytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@retaillytics.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2024 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks + a couple follow-ups after today's demo

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found the latency profiles and the prefetch description really helpful. A couple of quick follow-ups from our side as we start the Hosted API evaluation: 

- Rate limits: we saw the sandbox demo using ~120 rps bursts. For production, we expect intermittent bursts up to 350 rps for short windows. Can Hosted endpoints be configured to allow short burst capacity without overcommitting? Any recommended rate shaping?
- Endpoint mapping: we'd like one endpoint per feature (intent-classifier, summarizer, reranker). Do you recommend mapping those to separate model IDs or using query routing?
- Prefetch / KV caching: can you share the quickstart checklist for prefetch configuration and any sample TTL settings you recommend for retail query patterns?

Also attached is our traffic profile spreadsheet; apologies if some numbers are approximate.

Thanks,
Alec
Head of ML Engineering
Retaillytics

Attachment: Retaillytics_Traffic_Profile.xlsx (spreadsheet, 56KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alec Chen <alec@retaillytics.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@retaillytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2024 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + a couple follow-ups after today's demo

Alec — really glad it was useful. Quick answers below and I've attached the quickstart checklist you asked for. Will put together the short burst playbook as well and share by EOD.

1) Burst capacity / rate shaping:
- Hosted endpoints support "burst windows" via soft-burst policies; we recommend configuring a 60s burst envelope for predictable short peaks. For your pattern (350 rps short spikes), we suggest a baseline of 150 rps with a 60s burst allowance to 400 rps — this prevents dropped requests while keeping reserved compute reasonable.
- If you need guaranteed headroom, Dedicated is the alternative; but for many customers, soft bursts + queueing provide the desired balance.

2) Endpoint mapping:
- Best practice is to map logically distinct features to separate endpoints (and model variants) so you can tune batching and KV caches independently. For example: /v1/endpoints/intent-classifier -> smaller, faster model with lower latency; /v1/endpoints/summarizer -> larger model with higher token throughput.

3) Prefetch / KV caching quickstart:
- See attached Redwood_Quickstart_Checklist.pdf. TL;DR: enable prefix prefetch for stable context (product catalogs), set KV TTL to 10–30 minutes for catalog snapshots, and use per-endpoint caching with explicit invalidation hooks for deploy-time updates.

Next steps (proposed):
- We (Ben + Jordan) will draft a short burst playbook (rate windows, retry/backoff, circuit-break thresholds) and run it by your infra team.
- If you'd like, we can spin up a sandbox with endpoint partitions mapped to your three features and a couple of traffic-slice tests next week.

I'll attach the checklist and the playbook draft once it's ready.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Quickstart_Checklist.pdf (7 pages)

From: Priya Nair <priya@retaillytics.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2024 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + a couple follow-ups after today's demo

Thanks Mina — the checklist is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from our infra/security team: 

- For the soft-burst approach, what happens to requests that exceed the burst envelope? Do they queue, get 429s, or get routed to fallback model variants? We want predictable behavior so our client SDKs can implement sensible backoff.
- On endpoint mapping: will separate endpoints require separate API keys/scopes or can we enforce per-route quotas on the same key? We want per-feature throttles without splitting keys if possible.

Also, could you tack on a short section in the playbook about observability hooks (what metrics to expect during a burst vs sustained load)?

Thanks — Priya
VP Engineering, Retaillytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Nair <priya@retaillytics.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Alec Chen <alec@retaillytics.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2024 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + a couple follow-ups after today's demo

Priya — great questions; answering in order and adding the playbook items we'll include.

- Excess requests and degradation model:
  * Soft-burst envelope: excess requests will queue up briefly (sub-second to low-second depending on current load) and then be admitted if capacity becomes available. If queue + envelope capacity is exceeded, the runtime returns 429 with standard Retry-After headers. We typically recommend an exponential backoff with jitter in the SDK.
  * Automatic fallback: you can configure per-route fallback to a smaller, cheaper model for best-effort responses instead of 429s — the tradeoff is lower quality but improved success rate during sustained saturation. We'll add example configs in the playbook.

- Per-route quotas vs API keys:
  * You can keep a single API key and enforce per-route quotas and rate-limits centrally via the Redwood Console. This will let you maintain one credential while applying different token/second ceilings per endpoint. If your security policy requires key separation, we support that too — either approach works.

- Observability hooks to include in playbook:
  * Metrics: request_rate (rps), queue_depth, avg_latency_p50/p95, model_tokens_per_second, cache_hit_rate, fallback_rate, 429_rate.
  * Alerts: sustained queue_depth > 20 for >2m, p95 latency increase >50% vs baseline, fallback_rate >5% over a 10m window.

Planned immediate actions:
- Mina & Jordan: prepare a 1-page burst playbook with sample SDK backoff code and sample Console screenshots (deliverable: 2024-07-15).
- Ops trial: we can provision an endpoint partition with three endpoints mapped to your features for a 48-hour traffic slice next week (TBD dates).
- Doc: I'll upload the playbook draft, sample Console screenshots, and a short runbook for observability to the HubSpot deal and Google Drive.

If that aligns, Mina, can you confirm the sandbox dates and I'll raise the provisioning request? Priya/Alec — any constraints on the trial window (preferred days/times)?
